answer.rationale: With only 14 days before contract lapse and the line already at 94% of committed volume with no buffer, a full switch to the low-cost vendor (memory_c2) carries real delivery-risk exposure that isn't captured in that memory's onboarding/invoicing framing—it says nothing about ramp reliability under time pressure. Memory_c4 shows renegotiation at renewal has recovered real margin from this same incumbent before, and memory_c1 shows incumbent renewals have kept integration and delivery schedules stable. Given the primary objective is minimizing TCO without increasing delivery risk, attempting to negotiate the incumbent toward the mandate first preserves continuity while we still assess whether the low-cost vendor's quote reflects a real quality/reliability parity. I want to verify the original c2 record (was cost reduction net of any hidden delivery variance?) and c4 record (how much margin/price movement was actually achieved) before committing further, since only one sourcing decision is possible this cycle and switching is harder to reverse than negotiating.
